items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: And it was with Percy Heath and Connie Kay — not a bad rhythm section.

ctx.x: Oh, well. All right. That’s another story. This is, I’ve been in the country two weeks, no a week, and my wife and I, we’d run out of money because we’d stayed in a hotel in New York and we said well we can’t live here, it’s too much money. So we found an apartment in Brooklyn. And I looked in the local paper, and I saw there was a concert by the Modern Jazz Quartet at Brooklyn Academy of Music. So I said, I’ve got to try, I love those guys. You know I’d managed to hear it at some time. And so I got there very…

usually a kind of reserved guy, but I started getting into a conversation. And he said, “oh I know you.” I said, “how could you possibly know me?” He said, “well I subscribe to this English periodical it’s called ‘The Gramophone’ and they review jazz records. And you made a record in England and I have it.” I said, “what!” And I couldn’t believe it. He said, “by the way, what are you doing tomorrow night?” And believe me, I don’t make up these stories, it’s stranger than fiction. I said, “what do you mean, I’m…
Well what was the role with the, I mean, you were both piano players so what was he having—
